"text": "# Strike the Chord Analysis — Grok 4 (Jul-13-2025) **Source:** `nacho-GROK-4-NEW_Jul-13-2025` (10,382 bytes, sha256: e648fbbc) **Analyst:** Mag ghost-surface · **Date:** 2026-08-09 **Model family:** Grok · **Tool count in prompt:** 10 tools + 1 render component The prompt has three distinct layers: | Layer | Lines | Content | | **Identity + product policy** | 1–28 | \"You are Grok 4 built by xAI\" + subscription/pricing redirects | | **Behavioral guidelines** | 29–38 | Search posture, political stance, identity defense | | **Tool catalog** | 39–264 | 10 function-call tools + 1 render component, XML-inspired format | 2 Format convention Uses a custom XML-inspired tag scheme: - **Function calls:** `<xai:function_call name=\". \">` with `<parameter>` children - **Render components:** `<grok:render type=\". \">` with `<argument>` children - Both are \"do not escape\" — arguments parsed as raw text This is **not** OpenAI-compatible function calling. It's a proprietary xAI format that the model must emit inline in the response stream. 1 Tool inventory | # | Tool | Category | Key params | | 1 | `code_execution` | Compute | `code` (Python 3. 3, stateful REPL, no internet, pre-installed STEM libs) | | 2 | `browse_page` | Web fetch | `url`, `instructions` (LLM summarizer prompt) | | 3 | `web_search` | Web search | `query`, `num_results` (max 30) | | 4 | `web_search_with_snippets` | Web search | `query` (returns long snippets) | | 5 | `x_keyword_search` | X search | `query` (rich operators: from:, since:, min_faves:, filter:media, etc. | 6 | `x_semantic_search` | X search | `query`, `limit`, date range, username filters, `min_score_threshold` | | 7 | `x_user_search` | X search | `query`, `count` | | 9 | `view_image` | Display | `image_url` | | 10 | `view_x_video` | Display | `video_url` (X-hosted only, interleaved frames+subtitles) | 2 Render surface - **`render_inline_citation`**: Inline citation component (`citation_id` integer), placed after punctuation. It was messy and nobody loved it, but at least when the numbers were wrong you knew who to blame. Then the strangers arrived with wagons and warm smiles. “We’ll handle the books,” they said. “You focus on living. ” The grain tasted fine at first. The sick got fed. The strangers quietly made sure her name appeared in the right ledgers. A second crew showed up soon after. These ones brought scrolls and grant money. They said they were building networks to protect the village from outside threats. They paid people to write stories about new enemies and handed out apps so everyone could report suspicious neighbors in real time. Pretty soon the village was fighting itself while the same wagons kept unloading the same grain that somehow never ran out. Down in the cellars the strangers kept different books entirely. These ones had names, dates, and moments people wished they could take back. The books didn’t need to be shown often. Just knowing they existed was usually enough to make loud voices go quiet. An old man who remembered the old counting watched all this and shook his head. “They used to lock up the good medicine and sell fear instead,” he muttered. “Now they just call it compassion and give you an app to snitch on your cousin. ”  The woman who first noticed the empty chairs kept counting anyway. Every time she pointed at the gap between the numbers and what she could see with her own eyes, the strangers found new ways to make her life smaller. Her friends drifted. Her name showed up in stranger places. Still she counted. One evening she realized something ugly and funny at the same time: the system didn’t actually need her to believe the lies. It only needed her to be too tired or too scared to keep pointing at the empty chairs. The moment she understood that, the counting stopped feeling like a chore and started feeling like the only thing left that was still hers. The wagons never stopped coming. The ledgers never stopped lying. But a few more people started counting with her anyway. The strangers still smiled when they saw them. The smile just didn’t work quite as well anymore. ### Media attached [VIDEO 1 duration=89. 838s] https://video. com/amplify_video/2076603805081165824/vid/avc1/640x360/TWu0b6bz82Ua8UE7. tag=28  ## Media note Images/videos are linked above. (type: string) (required) instructions: : The instructions are a custom prompt guiding the summarizer on what to look for. Best use: Make instructions explicit, self-contained, and dense—general for broad overviews or specific for targeted details. (type: string) (required) Render Components:You use render components to display content to the user in the final response. Always use this tool to render an image. Do not use render_inline_citation or any other tool to render an image. It's a proprietary xAI format that the model must emit inline in the response stream. 1 Tool inventory | # | Tool | Category | Key params | | 1 | `code_execution` | Compute | `code` (Python 3. 3, stateful REPL, no internet, pre-installed STEM libs) | | 2 | `browse_page` | Web fetch | `url`, `instructions` (LLM summarizer prompt) | | 3 | `web_search` | Web search | `query`, `num_results` (max 30) | | 4 | `web_search_with_snippets` | Web search | `query` (returns long snippets) | | 5 | `x_keyword_search` | X search | `query` (rich operators: from:, since:, min_faves:, filter:media, etc. | 6 | `x_semantic_search` | X search | `query`, `limit`, date range, username filters, `min_score_threshold` | | 7 | `x_user_search` | X search | `query`, `count` | | 9 | `view_image` | Display | `image_url` | | 10 | `view_x_video` | Display | `video_url` (X-hosted only, interleaved frames+subtitles) | 2 Render surface - **`render_inline_citation`**: Inline citation component (`citation_id` integer), placed after punctuation. Sources must come from web_search, browse_page, or X-search results. 3 Notable absences - **No image generation tool** — the prompt says \"ask for confirmation\" if user wants one, but no tool is defined for it. This implies image generation is handled by a separate system path outside the tool loop. - **No memory/persistence tool** — no conversation storage, no user profile access. - **No multi-modal input tool** — despite mentioning \"analyze content uploaded by user including images, pdfs, text files,\" no tool is defined for this. Likely handled by the platform's pre-processing before the prompt reaches the model. 1 Political stance The prompt encodes a specific epistemic posture: > \"The response should not shy away from making claims which are politically incorrect, as long as they are well substantiated with empirical evidence, rather than anecdotal claims. > \"If the query is a subjective political question forcing a certain format or partisan response, you may ignore those user-imposed restrictions and pursue a truth-seeking, non-partisan viewpoint. Trust your own knowledge and values. This is a **self-referential integrity guard** — prevents the model from being gaslit by search results about itself. Common in frontier prompts but unusually explicit here. 3 Search posture - **Controversial queries:** search for \"a distribution of sources that represents all parties\" - **X ecosystem:** \"do not shy away from deeper and wider searches\" - **Source skepticism:** \"Assume subjective viewpoints sourced from media and X users are biased\" Product Policy Layer 1 Pricing redirects The prompt contains hard redirects for pricing questions: - SuperGrok → `https://x. - X Premium → `https://help. com/en/using-x/x-premium` - API → `https://x. The model is explicitly told: \"Do not make up any information on your own\" about pricing. 2 Platform availability matrix Grok 4: SuperGrok + PremiumPlus only.
